references.text: In the previous verse, the blind man cries out, "Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!" – the same cry he repeats with even greater force in verse 39, despite the crowd's attempt to silence him. See [ref:Luk 18:38|Luke 18:38].

In Matthew's parallel account of the two blind men at Jericho, exactly the same thing happens: the crowd rebukes them to be silent, but they only cry out even louder, "Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us!" See [ref:Matt 20:30-31|Matthew 20:30-31].

In Mark's account of Bartimaeus at Jericho, many rebuke him and tell him to be quiet, but he cries out even more, "Son of David, have mercy on me!" – a direct parallel to Luke 18:39. See [ref:Mark 10:47-48|Mark 10:47-48].

The Canaanite woman calls out to Jesus as "Son of David" and asks for mercy, while the disciples urge Jesus to send her away – but she does not give up. A similar pattern where some try to prevent someone from reaching Jesus, yet that person holds fast to their plea. See [ref:Matt 15:22-23|Matthew 15:22-23].

Earlier in the same chapter, the disciples rebuke those bringing little children to Jesus, but Jesus calls them to himself. This shows the recurring pattern in Luke 18 where people try to stop others from coming to Jesus, yet Jesus welcomes them anyway. See [ref:Luk 18:15-16|Luke 18:15-16].

Two blind men follow after Jesus and cry out, "Have mercy on us, Son of David!" – the messianic shout and plea for mercy that also the blind man in Luke 18:39 holds fast to. See [ref:Matt 9:27|Matthew 9:27].

The psalmist cries out to God and does not give up even though he receives no answer: "My God, I cry out by day, but you do not answer." This persistent endurance in prayer mirrors the blind man's refusal to be silent. See [ref:Sal 22:3|Psalms 22:3].

The parable of the unjust judge and the widow who does not give up, right at the beginning of this chapter, illustrates the value of persistent prayer – the same principle demonstrated by the blind man as he cries out even louder despite opposition. See [ref:Luk 18:1-8|Luke 18:1-8].
